text:
tanya: Heads-up 7 Enterprise customer (BlueCo) is pushing tenant routing + enterprise SSO into our v1 commitment. They called it a deal blocker and want dates.
mike: What does "enterprise SSO" cover for them?
tanya: OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and streaming audit logs to their SIEM.
lucy: Our published v1 target is July 20. BlueCo wants mid-June. That's a 4-6 week acceleration.
drew: If we accelerate, something must be deferred. Which items are least risky to slide?
vijay: Promo campaign widgets and extended analytics retention are safe candidates; low impact on core auth flows.
courtney: Eng estimate: OIDC + auth plumbing ~2-3w; SCIM ~4-5w (due to vendor syncs); audit streaming ~1w infra + 1w validation. Serially ~8-10w, parallel ~5-6w.
mike: SCIM is the biggest unknown (mapping HR systems, conflict resolution). OIDC + audit stream is a reasonable canary scope.
tanya: Proposal: offer BlueCo an OIDC-first canary (feature-flagged) by Jun 15 with audit export working, commit to SCIM GA by Jul 20. In exchange, move promo widgets & longer retention to v1.1.
lucy: Acceptance criteria for canary: successful login flow for 3 pilot tenants, audit events ingested by their SIEM, <1% auth errors, documented rollback.
drew: Infra note: run canary in single region, small dedicated pool, traffic only for pilot tenants. Need a short-lived CIDR route + KMS keys provisioned.
vijay: Legal: SLA language for enterprise can be a blocker. We should get counsel engaged immediately.
courtney: I'll draft a compact PRD and list the explicit cuts. Can take it to stakeholders today.
tanya: Action items: courtney -> PRD + cuts by EOD; lucy -> infra plan & canary routing by Thu; mike -> QA checklist & smoke tests by Thu; vijay -> legal SLA kickoff. I'll confirm canary acceptance with BlueCo after PRD.
triage-bot: Created SSO-9021 "blueco-sso-canary" and linked dependencies  https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/SSO-9021
tanya: Decision note (capture): deliver OIDC-canary targeted Jun 15 (feature-flagged, 3 pilots), SCIM GA in v1 targeted Jul 20. Cuts: promo widgets and extended analytics retention -> v1.1. Risks: SLA negotiation, SCIM vendor edge-cases.
mike: ack
lucy: ack
drew: ack
